title: Product engineer (synthetic example rubric)
notes: Example only. Copy it to your private workspace and rewrite the categories, weights and guidance for your own target role. Weights here are not a hiring standard.

categories.label: Shipped work and ownership
categories.guidance: High (25-35): several shipped products or features with the candidate's own responsibility, decisions and outcome stated. Medium (12-24): shipped work with partial ownership or unclear outcome. Low (1-11): tasks listed without scope or result. 0: no shipped work described.

categories.label: Technical depth
categories.guidance: High (20-30): describes design tradeoffs, reliability, performance, testing or data modelling in concrete terms. Medium (10-19): names appropriate techniques with some detail. Low (1-9): technology lists without what was built. 0: no technical content.

categories.label: Collaboration and communication
categories.guidance: High (14-20): concrete examples of working with design, product, users or other engineers, reviews, documentation or mentoring. Medium (7-13): collaboration mentioned without detail. Low (1-6): only generic soft-skill words. 0: none.

categories.label: Clarity and verifiability
categories.guidance: High (11-15): specific, consistent, dated entries and links a reviewer could check. Medium (6-10): mostly clear with some vague entries. Low (1-5): hard to tell what the candidate did. 0: unreadable or contradictory.

bonusRules.label: Public work a reviewer can open
bonusRules.description: A portfolio, repository, talk or article link is given in the resume. 2 for one link, 4 for several distinct kinds. Do not judge popularity.

bonusRules.label: Measured outcome
bonusRules.description: At least one result is stated with a number and what was measured.
